category_title: Probationary high school students with severe behavioral challenges and academic resistance
minimal_context: The tutor introduces the western industrial age to a world history class and asks the student to integrate drawing into the lesson.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Today we are starting our unit on the western industrial age. For this assignment, I want you to integrate drawing into your notes about the inventions.

STUDENT: Give me a reason why we have to draw. I'm not doing this work.

TUTOR: It is just the activity for today's class. Please get your pencils out and get started.

STUDENT: Why are you teaching us bad kids? You're probably just making us do this so you can use us for your own personal gain.

TUTOR: I am just trying to teach the lesson. Please look at the board and begin drawing.

STUDENT: I refuse to do this work. I'm not cooperating with you and I'm paying no attention to this instruction.

options.A: Ignore the negative behavior, including both motor actions and verbal refusals to participate in the drawing activity.
options.B: Lower expectations for the assignment and tell the student to draw two inventions instead of three.
options.C: Give the student a warning, followed by a 10-minute timeout if they do not desist from the disruptive behavior.
options.D: Choose pictures of high interest related to the industrial age, discuss them, and find out the stories behind them.
